mechanism: Builds or selects attention/GEMM/MoE kernels from dtype, head geometry, cache layout and workload metadata, with planned paged/ragged KV execution and specialized prefill/decode paths.
caveat: It is a multi-backend kernel library and generator rather than a standalone inference server, and support varies by feature and compute capability.

relevance_note: Reusable kernel foundation; isolates component reuse from claims of complete engine reconstruction.
target: At the checked HEAD, DeepSeek-V4.1 geometry, NVIDIA SM100/SM103 or Ascend 950, sparse indices and explicit FP8/FP4 KV layouts constrain the available kernels.
mechanism: Uses DeepSeek-specific latent/sparse-attention geometry, precomputed scheduler metadata and quantized KV layouts to run sparse decode/prefill and fused RoPE–attention paths.
caveat: The 2026-09-30 breaking release removed Hopper and earlier-model support and changed KV formats; old SM90/V3 descriptions apply only to the linked legacy commit. Fused RoPE paths have narrower backend support.

relevance_note: A model-and-device-specific runtime illustrates how narrow deployment contracts reshape implementation choices.
target: One model family and AMD gfx1151 unified-memory machines motivate tensor-specific precision choices and separate budgets for resident weights, KV state and the paged lookup table.
mechanism: Ships a model-and-chip-specific inference binary with mixed-precision weight layouts, a paged n-gram lookup table and dedicated attention/expert execution for Qwen3.8-Flash-Next.
caveat: The engine is distributed as a closed-source binary; public deployment files and quantization documentation cannot establish kernel implementation or all numerical-equivalence claims.

relevance_note: Reusable compiler foundation; compare which lowering and scheduling responsibilities a specialized stack retains or replaces.
target: NVIDIA GPU inference, operator coverage, task layouts and tuning-space size constrain the generated execution.
mechanism: Compiles PyTorch or ONNX graphs to CUDA kernels using graph rewrites, tunable operator schedules and explicit mappings from logical tasks to hardware workers.
caveat: Hidet is an optimizing compiler/backend rather than a deployment-specific serving engine; tuning and frontend compatibility must be evaluated for the chosen workload.

relevance_note: Reusable compiler/runtime foundation for target-specific programs and execution orchestration.
target: Hardware target, memory lifetime, asynchronous dependencies and the accepted input dialect constrain generated programs.
mechanism: Lowers MLIR programs into device executables and a runtime schedule, partitioning streamable work and planning resource lifetimes and allocations before deployment.
caveat: IREE is a general compiler/runtime toolkit; importing a model and selecting a target do not by themselves establish competitive model-level performance.

relevance_note: Reusable compiler foundation; compare which lowering and scheduling responsibilities a specialized stack retains or replaces.
target: PyTorch exportability, dynamic-shape representation, custom operations and compatible IREE compiler/runtime versions constrain deployment.
mechanism: Captures PyTorch modules or exported programs into IREE-compatible Torch IR, exposing AOT deployment, parameter handling and custom-operation integration.
caveat: Turbine is the PyTorch-to-IREE frontend and tooling layer, not an independent serving engine; the README warns that some dynamic-shape paths do not work with every head/release combination.

relevance_note: A native image-model runtime exposes which graph and execution responsibilities are taken out of a general framework.
target: Targets selected image-model architectures and local machines, with an optimized Apple Silicon path and CPU fallbacks.
mechanism: Implements selected FLUX and Z-Image pipelines in C with Metal or CPU kernels, memory-mapped weights and release of text encoders after conditioning.
caveat: Its supported architectures and precision paths are explicit; C implementation alone does not establish an end-to-end speed advantage over optimized frameworks.

relevance_note: Video inference framework route: compares breadth of model integration with narrower execution designs.
target: Targets large supported image and video models on memory-constrained accelerators and multi-device systems.
mechanism: Combines model-specific inference paths with quantized operators, cache policies, parallel execution and a two-slot block-loading system for overlapping offload.
caveat: Reported maximum speedups can combine runtime changes, quantization, step-distilled weights and lightweight VAEs, which need separate attribution.

relevance_note: General local-inference substrate and baseline; retained components must be distinguished from rewritten execution.
target: Checkpoint quantization type, tensor layout, matrix geometry, CPU instruction sets and accelerator memory determine eligible kernels and placement.
mechanism: Loads GGUF model tensors and executes a native GGML graph through backend-specific quantized kernels, dispatching by tensor type and geometry with optional CPU/GPU layer placement.
caveat: Backend and quantization support are not uniform across every operation or device; native low-bit execution does not imply identical accuracy or speed for all GGUF formats.

relevance_note: A dedicated inference stack exposes its kernel-composition and model-execution boundary for construction analysis.
target: Encoding, dtype, tensor geometry, layout, numerical contracts and target capabilities constrain kernel composition, while dynamic positions remain operands.
mechanism: Its inspected Metal/MLX path captures typed operations, selects compatible kernel plans and emits specialized fused Metal entry points inside MLX native compilation.
caveat: The concrete source audit covers the inference-v2 Metal/MLX path only; it does not establish identical specialization depth for CUDA, AMD or CPU backends or the advertised speedups.

relevance_note: MLX-based model implementation route: contrasts retained tensor framework with more extensive native reconstruction.
target: Primarily targets local Apple Silicon execution and explicitly supported MLX model implementations, with documented newer NVIDIA support.
mechanism: Implements selected image model components natively in MLX, with on-load low-bit weight quantization and optional adapter baking into inference weights.
caveat: Quantized checkpoints and adapter baking have format and precision constraints; a native MLX port is not evidence of universal speedup or identical outputs.

relevance_note: A model-to-persistent-program construction path connects generated execution schedules to a concrete runtime artifact.
target: NVIDIA GPU architecture, SM worker/scheduler allocation, model graph, batch shape and multi-GPU topology constrain the compiled execution.
mechanism: Compiles an explicitly assembled LLM task graph into a persistent CUDA megakernel whose GPU workers and schedulers execute computation and communication across decoding steps.
caveat: MPK requires supported task implementations and graph construction; its reported gains are workload-specific and are not an automatic guarantee for arbitrary Hugging Face models.

relevance_note: Compiler specialization route: establishes existing model-to-deployment construction and portability trade-offs.
target: Target device, model architecture, quantization, sequence bounds, tensor parallelism and low-batch workload determine compilation and runtime choices.
mechanism: Uses a TVM LLM-specific compilation pipeline to fuse dequantization and normalization, specialize low-batch GEMV, dispatch target-specific KV kernels and execute compiled models through MLCEngine.
caveat: This is a broad multi-platform compiler-backed LLM engine, not a separate hand-written runtime for each model; support and tuning remain backend-dependent.

relevance_note: Engine-building baseline with a closed optimizer/runtime core; compare disclosed interfaces and build cost.
target: NVIDIA devices, supported operators, precision contracts and min/opt/max input-shape profiles define an engine build.
mechanism: Builds NVIDIA inference engines specialized to optimization-profile shapes and selected kernel tactics, recording profiled decisions in a reusable editable timing cache.
caveat: The public repository contains plugins, parsers and samples, not the complete TensorRT optimizer/runtime core; internals beyond these interfaces were not inspected.

relevance_note: Compiler-backed pipeline adaptation: compares generated execution without reconstructing a full serving stack.
target: Requires a compatible compiler backend, PyTorch/CUDA versions and shape policy, with dynamic shapes trading specialization against recompilation.
mechanism: Converts diffusion-model modules into deployable compiled modules through OneFlow or Nexfort and reuses compiled graphs to reduce recurring inference overhead.
caveat: The inspected public adapter code delegates core compilation to backend packages; this audit did not establish that every backend component is public or current-version compatible.

relevance_note: General exported-model runtime baseline for portability and generation-state management.
target: ONNX model contracts, execution-provider policy, attention/convolution structure and KV quantization determine the state-management path.
mechanism: Executes ONNX generative models through execution providers while selecting model- and device-specific convolutional, shared, sliding-window or quantized KV-state managers.
caveat: This is a generative runtime on top of ONNX Runtime, not evidence that every execution provider accelerates every model or feature equally.

relevance_note: Framework compilation and capture route: compares incremental specialization and compilation amortization.
target: Targets NVIDIA GPU Diffusers pipelines whose repeated execution amortizes tracing and graph-capture costs.
mechanism: Traces Diffusers components into TorchScript, replaces common convolution/GEMM/GEGLU/normalization patterns with fused operators, and optionally captures CUDA graphs.
caveat: The README states active development is paused; traced graphs, lower-precision compute and backend compatibility require workload-specific validation.

relevance_note: Native diffusion framework route: compares existing cross-backend implementation and compatibility costs.
target: Targets multiple local CPU and GPU backends and models that fit supported GGUF and execution paths.
mechanism: Implements image and video diffusion in ggml-backed C/C++ with quantized weights, tiled VAE execution and architecture-gated sample-cache policies.
caveat: Cache modes and backend features are model-dependent; enabling a cache can alter outputs and is distinct from the native runtime rewrite.

relevance_note: Reusable execution backend for integration and comparison; component capability is separate from engine construction evidence.
target: C++/CUDA execution substrate used by DistServe and FastServe
mechanism: Provides transformer execution with paged attention, continuous batching and tensor/pipeline parallelism behind Python bindings.
caveat: Included as a concrete research backend dependency, not because of small code size; supported model families and software versions are limited.

relevance_note: A native Zig runtime exposes explicit model, format and platform contracts as a reconstruction boundary.
target: Explicit model–checkpoint-format–platform qualification, quantization group/bit metadata and memory admission restrict which execution paths are accepted.
mechanism: Executes a qualified set of model families from a native Zig binary using format-specific packed-weight readers and Metal/CUDA paths, fusing projections only when their packing contracts match.
caveat: The current 1.0.7 README describes a native serving runtime, so the older generic memory-virtualization label is stale; experimental readers and Living Weights must not be treated as generally qualified inference.

relevance_note: Reusable compiler foundation; compare which lowering and scheduling responsibilities a specialized stack retains or replaces.
target: Tensor metadata, chosen device backend and available schedule actions determine the captured and optimized execution.
mechanism: Fuses lazy tensor graphs, searches kernel schedules and captures compiled execution sequences with TinyJit for reusable memory-planned replay.
caveat: tinygrad is a full deep-learning stack with training support, not inherently a single-model inference engine; compact code size is not evidence of runtime superiority.

relevance_note: Reusable execution backend for integration and comparison; component capability is separate from engine construction evidence.
target: NVIDIA target hardware, TensorRT converter coverage, shape profiles and partition size constrain the delegated graph.
mechanism: Partitions exported PyTorch graphs into TensorRT-supported regions, compiles and caches those regions as engines and retains PyTorch execution for unsupported regions.
caveat: It depends on TensorRT and can produce mixed PyTorch/TensorRT execution rather than a completely standalone runtime.

relevance_note: Agent-guided fusion route: a narrower construction comparison with explicit verification and timing caveats.
target: The documented artifact targets selected models and an A800/SM80-oriented CUDA environment with model-specific fusion contracts.
mechanism: Combines LLM-guided ranking of bounded CUDA template candidates with contract-oriented fusion-kernel generation and an inference runtime.
caveat: The inspected generic verifier and selector contain skipped checks and proxy timing placeholders; README claims about strict validation or never-worse execution require separate verification of the specialized paths.

relevance_note: Agent-generated operator route: compares local code synthesis with integrated engine construction.
target: Target backend/DSL, device architecture, reference framework, precision tolerance and concurrent-search budget constrain generated operators.
mechanism: Generates and migrates accelerator kernels through multi-agent workflows, using UCB-based asynchronous candidate search and backend-specific verification and profiling workers.
caveat: AKG Agents is operator-generation infrastructure rather than a complete inference engine; backend readiness and the deprecated CLI must be distinguished from the current script/workflow APIs.

relevance_note: Evaluation and integration reference for testing generated components in model workloads.
target: Architecture-specific interfaces, captured production shapes, shared weights, task composition and target GPU determine candidate validity.
mechanism: Replaces candidate operators in production-shaped model pipelines and evaluates both kernel-level numerics/timing and end-to-end token outputs, throughput and latency.
caveat: FastKernels also exposes a minimal serving path, but its primary distinction here is integrated evaluation; kernel-level tolerance checks and exact greedy-token tests cover different contracts.

relevance_note: Reusable compiler foundation; compare which lowering and scheduling responsibilities a specialized stack retains or replaces.
target: Input shapes/strides, device backend, traceable operations and autotuning budget constrain each bound kernel.
mechanism: Compiles Python tile programs into GPU kernels and automatically searches tile sizes, indexing, loop order and launch strategies for bound tensor arguments.
caveat: Helion is a kernel authoring/compiler layer, not a serving runtime; first-use tuning can be substantial and optional agent source optimization is separate from the default configuration search.

relevance_note: Agent-generated kernel and composed-workload route: a construction comparison whose integration scope must be established.
target: Traceable workload structure, target GPU, shape signatures, reference tensors and search/refinement budgets constrain synthesized code.
mechanism: Decomposes PyTorch programs into fusable subgraphs, synthesizes Triton kernels, composes them back into a forward pass and iterates using correctness and hardware-profile feedback.
caveat: It targets kernel/program synthesis rather than a production serving stack; composition verification is an explicit option and finite tests are not a general correctness proof.

relevance_note: Operator evaluation foundation; local test success does not establish integrated engine validity.
target: Specified benchmark tasks, test-input generators, target GPU, numeric tolerances and measured baseline define what a score means.
mechanism: Compiles generated kernel implementations, compares them against PyTorch reference programs on randomized inputs and times only candidates that pass correctness checks.
caveat: This is an evaluation environment, not an inference runtime; finite task-level success or speedup does not establish deployment-level gains.

relevance_note: Connects a disclosed construction workflow to the VibeQwen engine case; the toolbox and generated engine are different artifacts.
target: Requested model, hardware, parallelism, precision, API contract and iteration budget define the generated artifact.
mechanism: Orchestrates coding agents to iteratively build deployment-specific inference servers, then launches fixed server contracts through correctness and performance oracle phases.
caveat: The inspected correctness oracle uses fixed prompts and LLM or heuristic judgments with hard/soft cases, which does not establish numerical equivalence to the original model.

relevance_note: Connects agent-guided optimization with inspectable model runtimes and their acceptance checks.
target: Model pipeline, GPU architecture, tensor shapes, denoising schedule, precision and perceptual-quality thresholds constrain accepted configurations.
mechanism: Composes model-specific video inference patches for fusion, invariant/cross-KV reuse, approximate denoising cache and sparse attention, with agent-guided configuration and visual-quality checks.
caveat: Exact implementation optimizations and approximate cache/sparsity/precision changes must be separated; model-specific code and quality checks do not guarantee bitwise equivalence.

relevance_note: Evaluation reference for matching speculative-decoding workloads and baseline conditions.
target: Comparing speculative decoding under matched devices and workloads
mechanism: Integrates draft/verification methods with shared task data, accepted-token statistics, timing reports and output-comparison scripts.
caveat: A benchmark artifact rather than a runtime; published leaderboard conditions do not validate unrelated hardware, checkpoints or serving loads.

relevance_note: Reusable compiler foundation; compare which lowering and scheduling responsibilities a specialized stack retains or replaces.
target: Device architecture, tile shapes, tensor-memory features, data precision and supported backend passes constrain generated kernels.
mechanism: Lowers tile-level kernel programs through target-specific layout and software-pipeline passes, generating GPU/accelerator code for tiled memory movement and matrix operations.
caveat: TileLang is a kernel DSL/compiler, not a full inference runtime; backend maturity differs and some targets deliberately disable unvalidated asynchronous pipeline paths.

relevance_note: Reusable compiler foundation; compare which lowering and scheduling responsibilities a specialized stack retains or replaces.
target: Target architecture, pointer/value signatures, compile-time constants, warp/stage counts and autotuning keys determine kernel variants.
mechanism: Compiles block-structured kernel programs for a selected GPU target and specializes cached binaries and autotuned launch configurations to argument signatures and compile-time constants.
caveat: Triton supplies kernel construction infrastructure; it does not supply model loading, serving policy or end-to-end inference correctness by itself.
